benefits.title: Students experience a more coherent and well-timed wider King’s experience
benefits.statement: Students encounter opportunities, support and invitations to participate at moments that better reflect their changing needs, capacity and priorities. Employability, student success, wellbeing, community, connection and wider participation are considered together around the student journey, creating clearer points of entry and re-entry and reducing the sense that different parts of King’s are competing for their attention.
benefits.successLooksLike: Students report that the wider King’s experience feels easier to navigate and better connected to the rhythms of their studies and lives. Participation and engagement are distributed more intentionally across the year, students encounter repeated opportunities to reconnect, and fewer periods are characterised by either competing institutional demands or limited invitation to engage.

benefits.title: King’s coordinates student-experience priorities more effectively around the student journey
benefits.statement: Stakeholders across employability, student success, wellbeing, community and connection, belonging, faculties, services and KCLSU plan increasingly from a shared understanding of student need and capacity. This makes intersections between agendas visible, reduces duplication and competition for attention, improves the timing and connection of existing provision, and provides a stronger basis for identifying gaps and commissioning selectively where new activity would add value.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, faculties, services, KCLSU and King’s
benefits.benefitType: institutional coordination and increased value from existing provision
benefits.successLooksLike: A shared student-journey planning rhythm is used by relevant stakeholders; major student-experience agendas are considered together at key planning points; competing demands, duplication and gaps are identified earlier; existing activity is coordinated more deliberately; and new commissioning is increasingly targeted at evidenced needs that cannot be met through better alignment of existing provision.
